answer: Sequential Work Witness. Each identity must publish a hash chain whose next link is only computable after solving a fresh challenge derived from the prior link, and peers timestamp chains at first sight. At dawn each day the network checks that no two identities share a chain prefix or timestamp cluster, rejecting late forks. Sybil cost: every clone needs its own real-time compute history, so N identities cost N times the sequential work, and any attempt to copy a chain summit fails the timestamp check. The signal is chain continuity, not registration.
